title: Reverse Quantum Annealing for Ground-State Energy Calculation in Molecule
abstract: We present the results of our reverse quantum annealing computations of the ground-state energies of alkaline-earth monofluoride molecules. By partitioning the Dirac--Coulomb electronic Hamiltonian into sub-QUBOs and refining forward-annealing solutions through optimized reverse-annealing schedules, residual configuration errors are systematically minimized. The electronic ground-state wave functions and energies are obtained using the Quantum Annealing Eigensolver algorithm. This work provides a pathway for achieving sub-milliHartree chemical accuracy and advancing molecular electronic structure calculations in the quantum annealing paradigm.
summary: This paper presents a method using Reverse Quantum Annealing (RQA) to calculate highly accurate ground-state energies for alkaline-earth monofluorides. By refining results from standard Quantum Annealing (FA) using optimized reversal schedules, the authors significantly reduce computational errors. This work advances the feasibility of using quantum annealers for high-precision molecular electronic structure calculations.
main_problem: The primary goal is to calculate the ground-state electronic energies of alkaline-earth monofluoride molecules with high chemical accuracy.
main_result: Reverse Quantum Annealing (RQA) systematically reduces residual errors from Forward Annealing (FA) by 82.3% to 98.1%, achieving sub-milliHartree accuracy when benchmarked against exact Full Configuration Interaction (FCI) results.
method: The study employs a hybrid quantum-classical approach, using the Quantum Annealing Eigensolver (QAE) algorithm refined by optimizing twelve different reverse-annealing schedules.
model_or_system: The system involves calculating the relativistic Dirac-Coulomb electronic Hamiltonian for molecules like BeF, MgF, CaF, SrF, and BaF. Calculations are performed in two active spaces: (3e, 8o) and (7e, 14o).
key_observables: Signed relative energy change ($\Delta E$), residual error ($\delta$) in milliHartrees (mHa), and the improvement metric ($\eta$) quantifying error reduction.
important_parameters: The performance is highly dependent on the chosen reversal depth ($s'$) and the specific annealing schedule ($S1-S12$), with optimal regimes found around $s' \approx 0.35-0.45$.
main_assumptions: The full QUBO is partitioned into smaller sub-QUBOs due to hardware constraints, and the final results are benchmarked against exact FCI diagonalization.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy profiles across the 12 tested annealing schedules for both the (3e, 8o) and (7e, 14o) active spaces, comparing FA, RA, and the FCI reference energy.
paper_structure: The paper details the mapping of the electronic Hamiltonian to a QUBO, describes the 8-step RQA protocol involving sub-QUBO partitioning and schedule application, and presents comparative results across different molecules and active spaces.
why_interesting: This work directly tackles the computational bottleneck in molecular electronic structure theory by demonstrating a quantum algorithm refinement (RQA) that pushes quantum annealers toward chemical accuracy for complex molecular systems.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Twelve reverse-annealing schedules evaluated in this work: (a) Pause schedules (S1–S5) with dwell intervals of 10, 25, and 40 µs at intermediate reversal points s′ ∈{0.35, 0.50, 0.65}; (b) V-shaped schedules (S6–S12) with a fixed total anneal time of 20 µs and reversal depths ranging from s′ = 0.35 to s′ = 0.65.

Figure 2. Computational architecture of the reverse-QAE algorithm. Left: Workflow schematic detailing the transformation from the relativistic Dirac–Coulomb Hamiltonian to the partitioned QUBO, forward annealing, multi-schedule reverse annealing, and continuous post-processing. Right: Algorithmic procedure executed across the normalization multiplier λ to obtain the variational ground-state energy.

Figure 3. Schedule-dependent RQA performance for (a) (3e, 8o) and (b) (7e, 14o) active spaces. Schedules are ordered monotonically from greatest average energy lowering to zero. Data points denote the mean signed relative energy change ∆E = (ERA −EFA)/|EFA| × 100, and error bars denote the standard deviation (±1σ) across the five molecular radicals. Sched- ule S11 (s′ = 0.40) achieves the highest mean energy lowering in both active spaces.

Figure 4. Molecule-averaged signed RQA energy change for (a) (3e, 8o) and (b) (7e, 14o) active spaces. Negative values denote variational energy lowering relative to the forward-annealing baseline. Error bars indicate the standard deviation across the twelve reverse-annealing schedules.

Figure 5. Benchmark of residual ground-state energy errors |E −EFCI| (in milliHartrees, logarithmic scale) relative to exact Full Configuration Interaction (FCI) for (a) (3e, 8o) and (b) (7e, 14o) active spaces. Forward annealing (FA, slate bars) leaves substantial residual configuration errors, whereas optimal reverse annealing (RA, colored bars) dramatically reduces the error by 82.3% to 98.1%, reaching sub-milliHartree chemical accuracy (< 1.594 mHa = 1.0 kcal/mol, dashed orange line) for BeF and SrF.
